subject.title: refactor(protocol): pre-publish cheat-window cleanup and vintage tracking

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally break the `question.*`, worker/catalog, and removed-export beta/pre-publication gateway-protocol contracts now, before public npm publication?
rationale: The patch deliberately changes wire and package API shapes across generated native clients and extensions; test success cannot determine which beta or future external consumers the project intends to support.

options.title: Confirm the pre-publication break window
options.body: Accept the documented beta/pre-publication compatibility boundary, require redacted end-to-end proof on the exact head, and merge once the remaining checks are green.

options.title: Preserve or migrate beta compatibility
options.body: Keep compatibility aliases or provide a scoped migration path for any beta clients or consumers the project still intends to support.

options.title: Pause the protocol freeze work
options.body: Defer these API removals and reshapes until a release-owner decision and consumer inventory are recorded.

recommendation.title: Confirm the pre-publication break window
recommendation.body: Accept the documented beta/pre-publication compatibility boundary, require redacted end-to-end proof on the exact head, and merge once the remaining checks are green.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR author is assigned to this broad protocol publication refactor and has authored its contract, generator, client, and CI changes.
